title: Introduce policy-ageing validator and audit-retention mapper
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a policy-ageing validator to prevent stale RBAC bindings from being accepted and a configurable audit-retention mapper that annotates audit events with retention buckets based on data residency and regulatory profiles.
description:
Context: This PR implements two complementary compliance controls requested by Governance and several SRE customers: (1) a policy-ageing validator that enforces explicit freshness on RBAC v2 bindings (prevents accepting bindings older than a configurable TTL unless explicitly renewed), and (2) an audit-retention mapper that annotates outgoing audit events with retention metadata based on tenant residency claims and KMS key-region scoping.

Motivation: customers operating under varying residency regulations required both signal-level TTL for bindings (to limit blast radius of long-lived grants) and stronger audit retention metadata to drive downstream retention enforcement (on log storage and export pipelines).

What changed:
- core/policy/ageing_validator.go: new validator that plugs into the policy admission pipeline. It verifies the binding.issued_at and binding.last_renewed timestamps, applies per-namespace and per-tenant TTL policies, and emits structured policy.validation_reason tags for observability.
- core/policy/ageing_validator_test.go: unit tests covering edge cases (missing timestamps, future timestamps, renew-within-grace).
- core/policy/config/config_schema.yaml: added policy.ageing.ttl defaults and per-tenant override knobs.
- audit/retention/mapper.go: new component that maps tenancy/residency claims + KMS key-region to a retention_bucket label (short, medium, long, sovereign). Mapper exposes a stable TTL and retention_policy_id that the log-forwarder consumes.
- audit/retention/mapper_integration_test.go: integration tests simulating cross-region keys and tenant claims.
- infra/helm/templates/audit-config.yaml: template flags to turn on mapper or set defaults per-environment.
- docs/security/policy-ageing-and-retention.md: design doc and operator runbook (rollback, migration steps, FAQ).
- small changes in k8s/webhook/deployment.yaml and tests to wire the validator into the admission webhook ordering.

Migration and rollout:
- Default behaviour is OFF for existing customers; flagged on per-org via feature-flag and config override.
- When enabled, the admission webhook rejects RBAC bindings that fail the TTL check with a clear error and guidance on renewal.
- A migration tool (scripts/migrate/renewal-assist.sh) is added to surface potentially stale bindings and allow bulk renew in a controlled window.

Security/KMS interactions:
- Mapper consults KMS key metadata (region and provider) via the existing kms/metadata client; if key metadata is unavailable, mapper will conservatively tag events as "unknown-region" and put them into a short retention bucket until operator review.
- Validator requires secure time (NTP) on control-plane nodes; added note in docs and a liveness probe to alert if time skew exceeds threshold.

Testing:
- Local unit/integration tests added; CI runs the policy and audit test suites (some tests previously flakey were hardened).
- Load testing: added a small canary harness that exercises the admission path with bursts (~1k rps) to ensure latency regression <5ms median.

Backwards compatibility & risks:
- No breaking API changes to user-facing endpoints.
- There is risk of accidental mass-reject if TTL defaults are set too low; mitigation: defaults off, and migration tool + dry-run mode.
- Mapper adds a new top-level audit label (retention_bucket); downstream log processors must ignore unknown labels (we added compatibility shims in the forwarder).

Docs & operator runbook:
- docs/security/policy-ageing-and-retention.md contains rollout checklist, helm values, troubleshooting tips, and sample renewal commands.

Related: Linear ENG-4052 (policy-aged-binding UX) and ENG-4091 (audit retention mapping).

operator_notes: Enable via helm value: policy.ageing.enabled=true and optionally policy.ageing.default_ttl_days=365. To perform a migration dry-run: scripts/migrate/renewal-assist.sh --dry-run --org=ORG_ID. Mapper keys: audit.retention_bucket values = [short, medium, long, sovereign, unknown-region]. Ensure log-forwarder version >= 1.12 to pick up compatibility_shim.
rollback_plan: Revert helm flags or set policy.ageing.enabled=false; run scripts/migrate/renewal-assist.sh --revert to restore annotated state; remove retention mapping by setting audit.retention.mapper=disabled and redeploy forwarders. Monitor metrics: policy.validator.rejected_count and audit.mapper.unmapped_count.
security_considerations: Validator enforces time-based rules; to avoid denial-of-service due to clock skew, nodes must run NTP. Mapper uses KMS metadata read-only; it does not alter keys. If KMS metadata fetch fails, mapper conservatively tags events as unknown-region rather than blocking audit writes. All new components are covered by existing RBAC for control-plane services.
notes_for_support: If a customer reports mass rejections after enabling: check policy.validator.dry_run mode, run renewal-assist.sh to list stale bindings, and escalate to SRE if more than 1% of bindings are stale across org. For retention mismatches, inspect audit.mapper.unmapped_count and KMS metadata availability via /admin/kms/metadata endpoint.
